entries.description: So these guys are experimental noise artists from the New York conceptual art/post-future scene. Each of them has a bunch of aliases (Rene Hell, Die Reihe), and they've both spent more than 20 years making really, really difficult-to-listen-to noise music. entries.title: /g/ Technology: What's the verdict on the Xbox consoles? It was an affordable way of playing Doo…
entries.description: What's the verdict on the Xbox consoles? It was an affordable way of playing Doom 3, Halo, Morrowind, KOTOR, etc. Xbox essentially shipped with a Pentium 3 733 MHz, 64MB DDR, a (slightly customized) Geforce 3, and an 8GB HDD for $299. A GeForce 3 was a pretty high-end card for 2001 too, a GeForce 2 and Directx 7 were really the standards still in 2001. Xbox OS was basically hyper-optimized Windows 2000, it's probably one of the most performant consumer-oriented x86 operating system ever written.

entries.title: /g/ Technology: How many email addresses are too many?

My main address that I use, my secondary for work / professional matters, a third for mobile apps to avoid cluttering up my main address, and a fourth for spam. Would it be worthwhile to make a separate address that I use solely for banking purposes or would that be far too many to deal with? entries.title: /g/ Technology: 12 V logic
entries.description: I've had a horrible epiphany.  AND and OR circuits with more than 2 inputs normally require exotic chips or wasteful cascades.  A Programmable Logic Device, pic related, will allow any function, of A, B, and C, by using a big OR with and AND of every permutation of A, B, and C.  Here is the epiphany:  You can configure a 555 timer as a Schmitt Trigger Not (Inverter).  This is the backbone of Mickey Mouse Logic: Using only diodes and a couple of resisters to create huge NAND, NOR, AND, OR, etc.
